name: Battle of Gestilren
summary: A Swedish dynastic battle in 1210 where Sverker II was defeated and killed by forces supporting Erik Knutsson.
details: A Swedish dynastic battle in 1210 where Sverker II was defeated and killed by forces supporting Erik Knutsson.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Battle of Gestilren was fought in 1210 during the dynastic struggle between the Sverker and Erik lines in Sweden. Sverker II was killed, and Erik Knutsson’s rule was secured.

contentSections.title: Background
paragraphs: Swedish kingship in the late twelfth and early thirteenth centuries was contested by rival royal houses. Earlier conflict at Lena in 1208 set the stage for the final confrontation.

contentSections.title: The battle
paragraphs: Details are sparse, but the result is clear: Sverker II died in battle and the Erik line prevailed.

contentSections.title: Aftermath
paragraphs: Erik Knutsson ruled as king after Gestilren, though dynastic conflict did not disappear from Swedish politics.

contentSections.title: Historical significance
paragraphs: Gestilren is important because it marks a decisive moment in the struggle between two royal houses during the consolidation of medieval Swedish kingship.

strength.note: This early-13th-century Swedish dynastic battle is barely documented; no army sizes are recorded.
Sverker II was killed here; the sources give no usable numbers for either side.

outcome: Result preserved in medieval narrative tradition; details vary by source.

imageInfo.caption: The granite memorial stone at Gestilren in Västergötland, raised in 1910 on the seven hundredth anniversary of the battle, in a 2006 photograph by Harri Blomberg.
imageInfo.creator: Harri Blomberg
imageInfo.note: Photograph of the memorial stone at Gestilren, in Varv parish in Tidaholm Municipality, Västergötland. Its carved inscription says that the people of Västergötland raised the stone in 1910, seven hundred years after the Battle of Gestilren, around the motto 'God save the Kingdom of Sweden'. It is a modern commemoration and shows nothing of the fighting of 1210. No depiction of the battle itself, medieval or modern, could be found on Wikimedia Commons: the Gestilren, Sverker II and Erik Knutsson files hold only coins, seals, heraldry and this monument, and the Swedish and English Wikipedia articles lead with the same photograph. Commons records the upload date, 25 August 2006, and no separate date taken. Licensed CC BY-SA 3.0.

battleContinuity.label: Another Scandinavian crown decided in battle
battleContinuity.reason: Sverker II fell at Gestilren contending for the Swedish throne, as Olaf II Haraldsson had fallen at Stiklestad contending for Norway's — kings killed in dynastic battles remembered chiefly through later narrative tradition.
